\looseness=-1 The main results reveal a core finding: \emph{unconditional correction is unreliable across suites}. CRM always-on applies the same learned residual to every step, including the ${\sim}$80--90\% of steps where the VLA is already confident. This produces inconsistent effects: $+$1.3\,pp on Spatial but $\Delta{\approx}0$ on Object ($77.8$\%, 2 seeds) and only $+$0.2\,pp on Goal. Corrections on confident steps are noise that dilutes gains on uncertain ones.

ACR-VLA avoids this by triggering CRM correction only on the minority of steps where the $K{=}2$ $L_2$ probe exceeds $\tau{=}0.25$ (trigger rate 4--20\%, varying with suite difficulty). On confident steps ($d_2 \leq \tau$), the pipeline outputs the argmin-to-centroid sample directly, adding zero perturbation. This selective application produces reliable positive effect across all suites: the CRM corrects where the VLA is uncertain while preserving the VLA's own output where it is confident.

The $K{=}10$ argmin baseline provides a complementary negative result: spending $10{\times}$ the inference budget on selection-only hurts on Goal ($-$2.7\,pp, 3 seeds). Multi-sample selection refines the action but cannot fix systematic errors in the VLA's output distribution. Learned correction is necessary, but only when gated.

\looseness=-2 We presented ACR-VLA, an adaptive inference-time correction pipeline for frozen flow-matching VLAs. A $K{=}2$ pairwise $L_2$ uncertainty probe ($\rho{=}0.9979$) gates a lightweight CRM (${\sim}$327K parameters). On SmolVLA (0.4B) across four LIBERO suites, ACR-VLA is the only method with positive improvement across all evaluated suites ($+$1.5--2.3\,pp), while unconditional CRM correction shows no benefit on Object ($\Delta{\approx}0$), $K{=}10$ argmin selection hurts on Goal ($-$2.7\,pp), and $K{=}2$ mean shows no improvement on Goal. The key finding is that adaptive gating---not correction strength---is the mechanism: correcting all steps adds noise on the ${\sim}$80--90\% of confident steps, negating gains on uncertain ones.
\textbf{Limitations.}\enspace Effect sizes are $+$1.5--2.3\,pp; the Spatial baseline is single-seed. The Goal improvement is statistically significant ($p<0.05$, 3 seeds). The CRM requires task-specific calibration data and stochastic sample diversity---deterministic VLAs produce near-identical samples and lie outside scope (Appendix~\ref{sec:applicability}). On Object, the two-seed ACR-VLA estimate ($79.3 \pm 2.5$\%) has high variance relative to its delta; additional seeds are needed to confirm significance. Broader cross-VLA generalization and real-robot transfer remain future work. AI tools assisted with code and manuscript.

1	Frozen Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models can be improved at inference time without modifying weights, but existing approaches either apply correction unconditionally or invest in multi-sample selection without learned correction.
2	We propose ACR-VLA, a lightweight adaptive correction pipeline for frozen flow-matching VLAs. At each control step, the pipeline draws $K{=}2$ action samples in a single batched forward pass and uses their pairwise $L_2$ distance ($\rho{=}0.9979$ vs.\ $K{=}10$ sample variance) as a per-step uncertainty gate. Low-uncertainty steps output the argmin-to-centroid sample directly; high-uncertainty steps apply bounded residual correction via a Correction Residual Module (CRM, ${\sim}$327K parameters). Batched $K{=}2$ matches single-sample latency (${\sim}$170\,ms), making the uncertainty signal computationally free.
3	On SmolVLA (0.4B) across four LIBERO suites, unconditional CRM correction is unstable ($+$1.3\,pp Spatial but $-$1.3\,pp Object). ACR-VLA's adaptive gate triggers correction only on high-uncertainty steps (4--20\%), improving performance where the VLA is uncertain ($+$2.3\,pp Spatial, $+$2.0\,pp Goal ($p<0.05$, 3 seeds)) while preserving baseline where the VLA is confident (Object, 3.5\% trigger rate)---avoiding unconditional correction's $-$1.3\,pp degradation. ACR-VLA uses $5{\times}$ fewer VLA forward passes than $K{=}10$ methods. The key finding is that \emph{gating}---knowing when to correct---is the mechanism: selective correction outperforms both unconditional correction and selection-only approaches. A boundary analysis on a deterministic VLA (OpenVLA-OFT 7B) confirms that stochastic action diversity is a prerequisite.

1	Frozen Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models can be improved at inference time without modifying weights, but existing approaches either apply correction unconditionally or invest in multi-sample selection without learned correction.
2	We propose ACR-VLA, a lightweight adaptive correction pipeline for frozen flow-matching VLAs. At each control step, the pipeline draws $K{=}2$ action samples in a single batched forward pass and uses their pairwise $L_2$ distance ($\rho{=}0.9979$ vs.\ $K{=}10$ sample variance) as a per-step uncertainty gate. Low-uncertainty steps output the argmin-to-centroid sample directly; high-uncertainty steps apply bounded residual correction via a Correction Residual Module (CRM, ${\sim}$327K parameters). Batched $K{=}2$ matches single-sample latency (${\sim}$170\,ms), making the uncertainty signal computationally free.
3	On SmolVLA (0.4B) across four LIBERO suites, unconditional CRM correction is unstable ($+$1.1\,pp Spatial but $-$1.3\,pp Object). ACR-VLA's adaptive gate triggers correction only on high-uncertainty steps (4--20\%), improving performance where the VLA is uncertain ($+$2.1\,pp Spatial, $+$1.3\,pp Goal, 3 seeds) while remaining neutral on Object ($\Delta{=}0.0$, gating correctly abstains)---avoiding unconditional correction's $-$1.3\,pp degradation. ACR-VLA uses $5{\times}$ fewer VLA forward passes than $K{=}10$ methods. The key finding is that \emph{gating}---knowing when to correct---is the mechanism: selective correction outperforms both unconditional correction and selection-only approaches. A boundary analysis on a deterministic VLA (OpenVLA-OFT 7B) confirms that stochastic action diversity is a prerequisite.
